newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa questions Boeing ties - report.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa questions Boeing ties - report.

text.p: The chairman of German airline Lufthansa AG was quoted on Thursday as saying its future procurement from Boeing Co could be affected by the U.S. group's plans to enter airline maintenance.

Juergen Weber was quoted by German business daily "Handelsblatt" as saying that such a move by Boeing would constitute "bad business behaviour". Lufthansa, traditionally a large Boeing client, is also a world leader in jet maintenance.
"If Boeing sets up in competition to us, it will have an impact on our future procurement. After all, we don't build airplanes," Weber was cited as telling journalists in New York.

Weber also hit out at "exclusive provider" relationships recently forged between Boeing and airlines such as AMR Corp's American Airlines and Delta, saying that Lufthansa would never enter such an arrangement.
"We shall continue to buy the best airplanes at the most favourable prices," he was quoted as saying.
